[b]Election year in Guagolandum: what to expect at the November 2027 election[/b]
[i]by María Roselli, [b]El Heraldo[/b][/i]

GUAGOFURK, JUNE 7 - Guagolandum has gone through a very interesting election year, full of political propaganda in all spheres of life. TV networks allocate no less than half of the advertisement spots in commercial breaks to political parties, and slogans are seen in billboards across Guagofurk and other major cities. Even people in small towns have begun to paint their walls or hang signs, often paid to do so by local branches of major parties. Incumbent Prime Minister José Luis Piñol, member of the Conservative Party, is running for re-election on a continuist platform supported by the Guagolandese center-right and right-wing while his major rival, Miguel Ángel Malatesta of the Social Democrats, runs on a progressive platform. A debate between the major candidates (Piñol, Malatesta, centrist Alfredo Márquez and unlikely catch-all populist Pablo Belcastro) was broadcast to the whole country three days ago, and the social media reaction in response to it resulted in a major rise in the polls for Belcastro, who went from near-unknown to polling above 10%. The election result is certainly shaping up to be a close call, and while Márquez lags a bit behind the rest, the race is certainly still ongoing.

According to recent polling, the main concerns of voters are foreign policy, specifically Guagolandum's reaction to intense political turmoil in Vespuria (especially concerning the recent events between Paldea and Rosenmarkke); domestic policy, primarily concerning government action against rising crime rates and poverty as big cities see previously unknown slums forming; and labor rights, primarily concerning a four-day work week and a significant raise of the minimum wage. Social issues are also at the forefront of this election, as the pro-abortion Social Democrats have promised to hold a national referendum on the issue, while the anti-abortion Conservatives have defended the current law regarding abortion legality (which limits availability to a few select cases).

The elections are taking place on 17 November 2027, and the latest poll conducted by El Heraldo with a total of 5,906 citizens nationwide has revealed the following results:

[b]29%[/b] intend to vote [b]Conservative[/b],
[b]28%[/b] intend to vote [b]Social Democrat[/b],
[b]11%[/b] intend to vote [b]Centrist/Moderate[/b],
[b]10%[/b] intend to vote [b]Loyalist[/b] (which is Belcastro's party),
[b]10%[/b] intend to vote [b]Liberal[/b],
[b]7%[/b] intend to vote [b]Socialist[/b],
[b]3%[/b] intend to vote [b]Green[/b],
[b]3%[/b] intend to vote [b]other political forces[/b].

[b][u]New Balion Empire's Exhibit at the World Expo: Dense Modern Living[/u][/b]
The New Balion Emperor himself has decided to send a pretty large delegation to the capital city of Tirakan, in order to show off the best of the Empire's urban infrastructure. Before the exhibit can be set up, a delegation led by Mr X and his team (with the exception of Mr G. Quagmire.... who landed in the nation and seemingly disappeared) is sent to the Government offices of Tirakan to formally set up relations between Tirakan and the New Balion Empire. It includes the gurantee of the NBE to formally recognise Tirakan and for their government to do the same for the Empire. Embassy details will include a team of 120 NBE officials within a central location of the capital and for Tirakan to set up a similar embassy in the Balion capital of Tandon.

The exhibit itself, a grand show of dense living is approximately the size of a medieval city (IRL medieval Paris) with around 250k Balionic citizens living in the dense environment while having modern amenities and quality of life. Built in the iconic "sky blue royal Balionic" style, the dense city shiny 7 storey tenement roofs can be spotted from miles away. Modern inventions such as sewers, electricity and other quality of life improvements are seen to be based on the outskirts of this mini city. A small overground railway system is put to circle above the city, showing that even yes, a dense city can be well travelled in. At the centre of the city, is a unique temporary Cathedral called "St Wood Pigeon's Pro-Cathedral" has been constructed to show off the latest in Church architecture. 

For the citizens themselves a stunning display of fashion has been shown off. In bright colourful and suave style for both men and women, the streets of this mini city is a bright array of colours from it's architecture to it's civilians. Along with this, also includes state of the art medical facilities, education centres and industrial progress all in one dense city. Overall, the city is proves that the once squalid and dense conditions of the Empire's inner cities where tens of millions reside in, can be improved for the better without slum clearances destroying historic and beautiful architecture and mass boring suburbia destroying natural environments. 

Along with the main exhibit of the dense city, the side exhibit from New Balion Empire is docked at the passenger port of the capital. It is one of the pleasure ships of the Empire and this one is called the "HMS Caligula", a 4 tunnel long ship (think Titanic irl) which at night, glows up in dark red. Despite many people thinking that the New Balion Empire is a prudish, reactionary state (well tbf it is still morally and socially conservative) an element of freedom is found upon this ship. With the latest technology and artistic sense, a wide array of romantic matters are found on this ship.

A security requirement is requested for the presence of local police to prevent any anti-Balionic peoples from disrupting the Empire's exhibits.

[i][b]Encrypted Message to [nation]Nordiheim[/nation][/b][/i]

It was the same bunker, the TIS used just a few days ago to contact Alaqar. The room was silent in a way that makes your thoughts, alongside to the white noise from the computers unbearably loud. There are no windos, flags, maps, or anything you could associate with Tirakan. But in the end of the room, a beamer lit up the wall with a projected picture of trade date between Nordiheim and Tirakan. Right next to that was a long list of infrastructure notification, reactor maintenance schedules and procurement channels. The data did not belong to Tirakan. The TIS had pored over these lists for months, to make sure that what they've expected since the 1990s already, is really true. Because making a mistake now, will cost the nations credibility. And many jobs. And many lifes.

"They built it the same way we did," said someone finally. It didn't really come off like an accusation. More like a conclusion, with a little bit of admiration.

"We've been suspecting it since decades now, what did you expect?", a man murmurs, leaned back in his seat, his legs rested on the table infront of him.

Nordiheims civil nuclear energy projects had always been public. They were transparent enough to satisfy the inspectors, opaque enough to allow for leeway. It was within such leeways that the truth had been uncovered by the TIS, but not with waterproof plans or documents, but in timing, in redundancies, in overlaps of procurement that only added up to one purpose if it wasnt energy production. To the TIS, figuring it out, was a pretty easy game. After all Tirakans own nuclear journey, begun unknowingly contemporaneous to Nordiheims, under the same cover of a civil nuclear energy project. The same idea, the same schedules, the same date. It was a reflection of exactly that, what the Tiraki Intelligence Service has been made for in the first place.

Suddenly the doors swing up, and two men in black suits followed by a handful of security guards march into the room. In shock both men, just casually chatting a second ago, take their feet off the desk and straighten up. Immediately a channel is opened, and projected onto the wall onto the end of the room. It was an old encryption line agreed upon with Nordiheim, for emergencies years before the civil war kicked off. After all men inside the room watch the bar load to its fullest once, one man in suite, TIS general director Ahman Befir, stepped forward, and the personell immediately took seat behind dimly glowing PC screens. 

"All set?", he asked and cleared his throat after a nodding response from both men next to him ready to type down his words.

[b][ENCRYPTED TRANSMISSION TO NORDIHEIM - MIDGARD][/b]

To the highest council of Nordiheim,

This message is sent with the expectation of discretion. Its existence is not intended for acknowledgment beyond the recipients of this channel.

Tirakan has, over the course of decades, maintained close commercial and technical relations with Nordiheim. Through these relations, and through long-term observation rather than intrusion or distrust, we have come to understand that our two states share more than trade corridors.

Tirakan is aware that Nordiheim has, since the late 1980s, maintained a nuclear weapons program concealed beneath the framework of its civil nuclear energy sector. This awareness is not the result of a single incident, breach, or disclosure, but of experienced pattern recognition conducted over many years. We state this plainly so there is no misunderstanding.

Tirakan has walked the same path.

We contact you, to reveal that Tirakan too, is attempting to develop nuclear weapons, in the face of modern days threats. Our own nuclear weapons program began in 1988. It survived years of internal compartmentalization, and later, disruption caused by civil war. During that period, the Free Republic of Naerim, which was the faction reunifying the country and re-newing the Nordiheim-Tirakan trade pact, retained control of key facilities and accelerated development out of necessity rather than ambition. Today, Tirakan has regained political stability, and our program has entered its final developmental phase.

We are contacting Nordiheim now because circumstances have changed. In the face of international pressure, nations attempting to reveal the truth behind Tirakans nuclear weapons program, silence will not bring us far in certainty. It is inefficiency, that we've been willing to endure facing no time pressure. But this has ended now.

We believe both our states face the same reality. Pursuing nuclear deterrence alone increases risk and vulnerability. Cooperation, even if limited, reduces both.

Tirakan therefore proposes covert cooperation between our nuclear weapons programs, specifically in areas where parallel development has already occurred and mutual benefit is evident. This cooperation would be strictly secret, state-to-state, and restricted to a minimal circle of trusted scientific and strategic authorities. Nothing public.

If Nordiheim is willing to explore this cooperation, we request confirmation through this channel only. Further structure and safeguards can be discussed once intent is established.

If you choose not to respond, this message will not be repeated and never to be found again.

My name is Ahman Befir, general director of the Tiraki Intelligence service. 
I talk in the name of my country: We expect your response soon.

[b][TRANSMISSION ENDS][/b]
